cases.text: MISO is a hierarchical neural implicit SLAM back-end coupling residual-conditioned local initialization with global submap alignment and fusion. Within multiresolution feature-grid submaps, fixed pretrained encoders initialize finer grids from residuals left by coarser predictions; grid features and robot poses are then jointly optimized with a fixed shared decoder. Global optimization aligns overlapping feature fields from coarse to fine without decoding SDF values during feature-alignment iterations, then refines poses using SDF disagreement. Fusion averages aligned implicit features before decoding, rather than averaging decoded SDFs. On ScanNet 0011, from initial submap errors of 5 degrees and 0.20 m, alignment takes 10.53 s versus MIPS's 59.23 s, with final errors of 1.86 degrees/0.06 m versus 3.93 degrees/0.15 m. Evaluation is predominantly offline on static scenes, and dense grids limit memory scalability.
cases.note: Retained local initialization followed by joint optimization and both global feature-space operations; scoped the comparison to ScanNet 0011 and preserved the offline/static evaluation boundary.

cases.text: We present XM, a certifiable scaled bundle-adjustment solver that jointly estimates camera poses, landmarks, and per-frame depth scales. Learned depth lifts matched image points into camera-frame 3D measurements; frame scales adjust these measurements before alignment with global landmarks. An empirically tight semidefinite relaxation supplies optimality bounds, while a low-rank Riemannian staircase and C++/CUDA trust-region implementation make optimization scalable. Dual checks certify relaxation solutions or trigger rank increases and descent, rather than accepting an uncertified local factor optimum. XM-SfM combines XM with matching and outlier filtering, then uses its estimates to initialize CERES refinement of the original reprojection objective. On BAL-1934, using the same lifted 3D observations, XM and MANOPT require 2.09 and 236.46 s of solver time, respectively, excluding 69.15 s of preprocessing for each.
cases.note: Distinguished relaxation certification from downstream reprojection refinement and solver timing from preprocessing; retained the staircase and C++/CUDA implementation as computational co-contributions.
